prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Evidence is still thin for adoption redesign, finish new_screen, finish new_flow, and sign_in hint changes, as no kind of change has at least 2 tests yet.
No kind of change has been shown to be helpful yet, as all tests so far resulted in no clear effect.
Predictions were consistently too high across all tests, particularly for redesigns (predicted +12.0%, measured -3.4%) and new flows (predicted +2.0%, measured -4.6%).

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, redesign: -1.4% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, new_flow: -2.0% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, new_screen: +1.1% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, hint: +0.1% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 17.8%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [finish, new_screen] Desktop Controls Quick Reference Screen: Adds a static quick reference screen after home intro showing fundamental desktop pet mouse controls. (why: Support receives multiple emails from users confused about how to interact with, hide, or control their pet after finishing onboarding.)
1: [adoption, redesign] Grid Layout for Pet Friend Selection: Redesigns the pet selection screen layout into a clean grid view displaying available companions side-by-side. (why: Adoption has a 39.1% drop-off rate and a high median decision time of 89 seconds.)
2: [home, new_flow] Pre-Hatch Desktop Tips Wait Screen: Adds an informational tips screen right before the main waiting screen to set expectations while generation takes place. (why: The home wait screen suffers from a mean duration of over 38 minutes and 18.7% user drop-off.)
3: [choose_path, redesign] Two Column Path Selection Layout: Redesigns the choose_path screen into a two-column comparison card layout. (why: Choose path drops 23.8% of users with an average duration of 514 seconds.)
4: [sign_in, hint] Sign-In Sync Explanation Hint: Adds explicit hint text on the sign-in screen explaining that signing in syncs pet state safely to cloud storage. (why: 8 support emails complained about missing or reset pets after signing back into their account.)
5: [home, wait_info] Background Wait Desktop Notification Toggle: Enables background desktop notifications on the waiting screen with clarifying helper copy. (why: Mean wait time is 2336 seconds, causing users to abandon the app while generation finishes in the background.)
6: [choose_path, copy] Story Screen Value Copy Refresh: Updates story screen text to emphasize low-overhead background desktop companionship. (why: First step drop-off is 23.8% right at the beginning of onboarding.)
7: [finish, copy] Desktop Visibility Reassurance Copy: Updates home_intro headline and hint reassuring users where on their monitor to look for their pet. (why: 3 support tickets reported users believing the pet did not spawn on their desktop.)
8: [sign_in, copy] Sign-In Troubleshooting Guidance: Adds explicit troubleshooting helper copy to the sign-in screen body. (why: 2 support tickets noted that the sign-in prompt failed to appear or stalled.)
